# @apodemakeles/dsh-token-dashboard
English | 中文
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) web GUI plugin: a token-consumption heatmap panel. It shows your **total to
ken usage per day / per week** across all projects on this machine, GitHub-contributions style. Usag
e facts are projected into a local SQLite database by a persistent Worker, so opening the panel neve
r scans session logs.
> Status: **released v0.2.0** — GitHub distribution is live. The package is not currently published
s: **released v0.2.0** — GitHub distribution is live. The package is not currently published to npm.

## What it does
- **Host half** — listens to live `session/event`, flushes through DSH's durability barrier, and sen
ds minimal usage deltas to a persistent Worker. The Worker owns SQLite (`node:sqlite`), commits fact

s/checkpoints atomically, and serves one consistent snapshot endpoint.
- **Client half** — puts a li
ve **today capsule** in the sidebar footer (`● 今日 478.9k tokens`): today's total, always visible wit
hout opening anything, refreshed by one cheap `weeks=1` snapshot read on mount, on window focus, whe
n the panel closes, and every 30s while the window is visible. Clicking it opens the panel — weekly
heatmap grid + daily view — which fetches a single `GET /api/token-dashboard/snapshot` per open/refr

esh/page change.
- **CLI** — `dsh-token-dashboard status|verify|rebuild|backups|restore|cleanup` for
**CLI** — `dsh-token-dashboard status|verify|rebuild|backups|restore|cleanup` for local maintenance.
## Installation
The plugin is one package with two halves and no runtime dependencies; it runs on the DSH **web** pr
ofile and in the official **DeepSeek Harness desktop app** (which boots the same web App inside Elec
tron on its own `desktop` profile).

## Data and operations

- Projection database: `$DSH_HOME/data/token-dashboard/usage-v1.sqlite` (default `~/.dsh`).
- Profil
es share one Harness home, so the desktop app and `dsh web` read the **same** database and the same
`$DSH_HOME/sessions` logs: history collected under one profile shows up under the other with no migr

ation step.
- Total tokens = `inputTokens + outputTokens + cacheReadTokens` (cache reads count into

the headline).
- The panel only calls the snapshot route; it does not trigger a session listing, `in

spect`, a source read, `flush`, or backfill.
- First startup initializes the database in the backgro

und; the panel shows phase/progress until `ready`.
- A session log the running harness cannot interp
ret (for example a pre-release subagent log whose child descriptors are no longer readable) is isola
ted: it is listed on stderr with its reason, the phase ends `degraded` instead of `ready`, and the f
acts already committed for it stay in the database.

## Known limitations
- Projection is machine-local: it reads sessions stored on this machine (`~/.dsh/sessions` is the au

thority; SQLite is a rebuildable projection).
- Host/Worker changes require restarting DSH; client H

MR does not cover the persistent Worker.
- SQLite is experimental in Node 24 (`node:sqlite`); the pl
ugin checks capability at startup and does not hide the warning globally.
